sentences.text: Exploring a research collaboration on KCNT1-related disorders
We are writing to the KCNT1 Epilepsy Foundation, and would also value the views of the Rare Epilepsy Network.
KCNT1-related disorders are linked to gain of function, where the channel does too much.
The KCNT1 International Registry and Citizen Health include people with these disorders, and a KCNT1 natural history study has been completed.
A registry and a survey study of epilepsy-dyskinesia syndromes are recruiting, as are early trials of S230815 and ABS-1230.
Two approaches are contested: an antisense oligonucleotide was linked to ventricular enlargement or hydrocephalus in both treated infants.
Quinidine showed no efficacy in a small trial in ADNFLE, despite case reports of seizure reduction.
We would like to explore a jointly designed study on KCNT1-related disorders, shaped with your community from the start: [study question], [design], [sites].
Any participation would follow informed consent and ethics approval, and we would share what we learn with your community.

sections.heading: What we would ask of you

sentences.text: Would you be open to a conversation about whether this idea is useful to the families you serve?
If so, we would value your view on how your community, registry or natural history work could take part, with proper consent and ethics approval.
We are not asking for any personal information about patients or families.
Could we arrange a short call at a time that suits you, perhaps [proposed dates]?
With thanks and warm regards, [researcher name], [institution].
